title: QUIZ - 86
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the result of exponential growth over several time periods
questions.question: A population starts at 29 and grows by 5% each year. What is the population after 3 years (rounded to the nearest whole number)?
questions.explanation: Exponential growth follows \(P = P_0(1+r)^t = 29(1 + 0.05)^3 \approx 34\).
questions.hint: Exponential growth multiplies by (1 + rate) repeatedly, once per time period — it does not simply add the same amount each time.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize a real-world scenario that follows exponential rather than linear growth
questions.question: Which scenario grows by a constant multiplying factor, rather than a constant fixed amount?

options.label: A
options.text: A candle that burns down by exactly 6 cm every hour.

options.label: B
options.text: A savings account that gains exactly $60 every month.

options.label: C
options.text: A viral video whose view count triples every 6 days.

options.label: D
options.text: A wall that is painted 6 square meters every hour.

questions.explanation: "A viral video whose view count triples every 6 days." grows in proportion to its current size, which is the defining feature of exponential growth, unlike the other options, which add a fixed amount each period (linear growth).
questions.hint: Exponential growth means the quantity is multiplied by a constant factor each period, not increased by a fixed amount.

questions.concept: Comparing Exponential and Linear Growth Over Time
questions.learningObjective: Compare the outcomes of linear versus exponential growth models after several time periods
questions.question: A quantity starts at 29. Model A grows by adding 3 each year (linear); Model B grows by 10% each year (exponential). After 6 years, which model gives a larger value?

options.label: A
options.text: Both models give exactly the same value.

options.label: B
options.text: Model A (linear), because the fixed addition is larger at this point.

options.label: C
options.text: Model B (exponential), because percentage growth compounds over time.

options.label: D
options.text: This cannot be determined without a graph.

questions.explanation: Model A gives \(29 + 3 \times 6 = 47\). Model B gives \(29(1+0.1)^{6} \approx 51\). Comparing these values determines which is larger.
questions.hint: Exponential growth compounds on itself over time, so it eventually outpaces linear growth, though not always immediately.
